newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita aims for A, B share dividends '96.
newsitem.headline: Merita aims for A, B share dividends '96.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said on Thursday it aimed to pay dividend on its preferential B shares and a modest dividend also on its A shares on its 1996 result.
"It is our aim that the result for 1996 will permit us to resume payment of dividend," it said in a statement with its January-September interim results.
"B shares carry preferential rights in this respect, but we believe it will be possible to declare a modest dividend also on A shares if the economy remains on the present course."
Of the banking groups that formed Merita in 1995, Unitas last paid a dividend on its 1991 results and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki in 1990.
Merita said its aim to pay dividends for 1996 would not be jeopardised by occasional turbulence on the money or stock markets in the final quarter.
Merita repeated an earlier forecast that it had strong possibilities for a clearly positive result in 1996 and said there were chances for further improvement next year.
"Given the continuation of economic growth, the necessary pre-conditions will exsist for a further improvement in results next year even assuming a flat trend in lending," it said.
